reputation.summary: Not web-verified. Reportedly a vintage BiFET dual in 1980s–90s consumer and synth gear, called smooth or warm by some listeners and ordinary by measurement-minded reviewers. On paper it is TL072-class (16–18 nV/√Hz, 3–4 MHz). TI lists pro audio mixers; National specified THD <0.02%. Its appeal is originality in restorations.
typical_uses: Vintage preamp, tone-control and filter stages (unverified)
Active filters, integrators, sample-and-hold, D/A converters
Budget Chinese DACs, e.g. Xiang Sheng DAC-01A (low confidence)
caveats: Noisier than bipolar duals: 16–18 nV/√Hz vs about 5 for NE5532; matters with low-impedance sources.
Offset up to 10 mV (13 mV over temperature): trim, servo or AC-couple DC stages.
Phase reversal below the negative CM limit (National): keep inputs 3–4 V above V−; below V− can destroy it.
Output specified only into 2 kΩ/10 kΩ: not for 600 Ω or headphones. Commercial 0–70 °C only.
Specs differ by vendor and TI lineage: LF353P (3 MHz/18 nV) is not LF353M/NOPB (4 MHz/16 nV).

counterfeit_notes: No LF353-specific reports checked. A cheap commodity part, but recycled DIP pulls are common. Buy TI or ST stock from authorised distributors. 'New' ON-marked stock is old (discontinued c. 1999–2000). LF353AN/BN or TO-99 LF353H parts are pre-2000 National.

silicon_changes.vendor: Texas Instruments (TI's own LF353, SLOS012 lineage; not the ex-National LF353-N)
part_numbers_affected: LF353P / LF353PE4 (likely; not itemised in any retrieved source)
silicon_changes.identification: Unchanged part number, marking and datasheet (SLOS012C). Identify by date code after first ship 2022-09-16. Die rev C/E/F/H → A. LF353-N (National design) unaffected.
silicon_changes.summary: TI moved its own LF353 from Sherman to RFAB with an entirely new design (PCNs 20220615003.1, 20230627002.1). E2E 1512001: guaranteed limits unchanged. E2E 1442987: bandwidth rose to about 4.5 MHz, risking instability. The TL082's new die adds VCC+ clamps (E2E 1428797); unconfirmed for LF353.

spec_deltas.after: about 4.5 MHz (TI E2E statement; not a datasheet value)

spec_deltas.before: no clamp to V+ reported (legacy die)
spec_deltas.after: clamp diodes to VCC+ reported for the same PCN's TL082 new die; unconfirmed for LF353

spec_deltas.parameter: Slew rate / input bias / supply current (typ)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: About 50% more real bandwidth changes phase margin in filters, followers and cable drivers. Vintage circuits may oscillate; ~10 pF across 30 kΩ fixed one.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - pin-compatible, same limits, but an entirely new die with ~50% more bandwidth.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN dates (samples to 2022-07-16) and E2E statements confirmed; 20230627002.1 (reportedly 2023-10-25) covers LF353DR.

part_numbers_affected: LF347 (other TI LF347/LF347B orderables not confirmed)
silicon_changes.identification: Unchanged part number; no marking or die letter known. Identify by date code after first ship 2023-03-20 (samples to 2023-01-20). LF347-N/LF147 not implicated.
silicon_changes.summary: The TL072/TL074 RFAB notice lists LF347N and LF347 in Group 2: 'RFAB/Process migration and adding MLA Assembly site'. TL07x got a revised die; for LF347 no die letter, datasheet delta or user report was found. Links to PCNs 20220615003.1 and 20230627002.1 are unconfirmed.

spec_deltas.before: legacy fab (Sherman, per the sibling TL07x/LF353 moves)

spec_deltas.after: MLA added as an assembly site option

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. If it follows the TL07x/LF353 RFAB dies, expect different bandwidth, slew and input behaviour in legacy mixers and synths.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - RFAB migration is PCN-listed; actual electrical deltas and die status unknown.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN summaries list LF347N/LF347 in Group 2. No E2E report, die letter or datasheet revision found.

silicon_changes.vendor: Texas Instruments / National Semiconductor (two TI product lines)
silicon_changes.identification: TI: LF353P/DR/D/PE4, SLOS012, 3 MHz. National: LF353N/M/MX (/NOPB), DS005649 or SNOSBH3F (revised March 2013), 4 MHz. Pre-2011 National parts carry the NS logo.
silicon_changes.summary: TI sells two LF353 products. National's (TI LF353-N): 4 MHz, 16 nV/√Hz, THD <0.02%. TI's own, likely its own die: 3 MHz, 18 nV/√Hz, no THD figure, like its TL07x. DC specs and 13 V/µs match. TI's LF353 is now a new RFAB die, so the gap may have changed.

spec_deltas.before: 4 MHz (2.7 MHz min), National DS005649 / TI SNOSBH3F
spec_deltas.after: 3 MHz typ, no min, TI SLOS012C
18 nV/rtHz, RS = 20 ohm (TI Rev C; RS = 100 ohm in 1988)

spec_deltas.before: normal operation on +/-6 V (National application hints)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Probably small: the National version is specified slightly quieter and wider-band, with a THD guarantee. Both are TL072-class.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same pinout, function and DC specs; only minor AC-spec differences
silicon_changes.verification: RS lists LF353P at 3 MHz and the /NOPB parts at 4 MHz; TI keeps separate LF353 and LF353-N pages.

silicon_changes.identification: Parts marked LF353AN/BN, LF353AH/BH (TO-99 can) or LF351A/B are pre-2000 National. The 2000 sheet lists only LF353M/MX/N.
silicon_changes.summary: National dropped the A/B offset grades and the TO-99 can, added SO-8, a 2.7 MHz GBW minimum and an ESD rating, raised Tj(max) from 115 to 150 °C and cut N-package θJA from 160 to 115 °C/W. New-format DS005649 first dated April 1998. No die change documented.

spec_deltas.before: LF353A 2 mV / LF353B 5 mV / LF353 10 mV max

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None documented. The A/B grades differ only in offset.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same die family and pinout; the TO-99 can has a different footprint
silicon_changes.verification: Based on the 1980 and 2000 National datasheets cited.

silicon_changes.identification: TI: 'LF347, LF347B JFET-Input Quad Operational Amplifiers', SLOS013, 3 MHz. National: 'LF147, LF347-N', SNOSBH1D, 4 MHz typ / 2.2 MHz min.
silicon_changes.summary: TI keeps two quad lineages: its own LF347/LF347B (SLOS013C, March 2016) and the ex-National LF147/LF347-N (SNOSBH1D, March 2013). The claim that TI's LF347 documentation moved to the National design is refuted: lf347.pdf and gpn/LF347 serve SLOS013.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown; both are TL074-class BiFET quads.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same function and pinout (LM348-compatible per TI SLOS013B)
silicon_changes.verification: gpn/LF347 serves the TI-lineage title; a separate LF347-N product page exists.

silicon_changes.identification: ST logo and ST orderables (LF353DT, and LF253 industrial grade). One ST datasheet (Doc ID 2153) covers LF253 and LF353.
silicon_changes.summary: ST specifies its LF353 as 4 MHz, 16 V/µs, 15 nV/√Hz with a 0.01% THD headline. ST's selector gives its LF35x and TL072 the same 1400 µA/ch, hinting at a shared JFET process (unverified). Mouser's LF353DT figure (3.2 mA per package) differs.

spec_deltas.after: 1.4 mA/ch (ST selector) or 3.2 mA typ per LF353DT (Mouser)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Marginal. ST's version is slightly quieter and faster on paper.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: drop-in, but ST's LF353 is rated only to 32 V against TI's 36 V
silicon_changes.verification: ST LF253/LF353 Doc ID 2153 Rev 3 (March 2010) confirmed.
